quotes.text: A record is official evidence that your organization did something, decided something, approved something, or agreed to something.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Plain-language definition of what makes a file a record.

quotes.text: You can use both approaches in the same connected platform, but they solve different problems. Policies handle broad coverage, while labels handle the records that need individual treatment.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clarifies the common confusion between retention policies and labels.

quotes.text: These tools can work together, but they shouldn't be confused. One protects the document while people use it and the other protects the business obligation across time.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Separates information protection from records management.

quotes.text: Assign reviewers through a maintained group when you can instead of naming one person. People change jobs, they take leave, they leave the company.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Practical setup advice that prevents stalled disposition queues.

quotes.text: If someone challenged a deletion years from now, could your organization show the rule, the approval, and the recorded activity that led to it?
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A concise test for defensible records governance.

chapters.title: Intro: from filing cabinets to Microsoft 365
What counts as an official record
Retention labels are the rule book
Disposition review: the gate before deletion

takeaways: Microsoft Purview Records Management keeps official records for the required time and disposes of them in a controlled, reviewable way.
Retention labels attach item-level rules (trigger, period, end action), record declaration locks official evidence, and retention policies cover broad locations.
Disposition review and Purview Audit provide the decision gate and the trail needed to prove why a record was kept or deleted.
hook: Contracts, policies and financial reports now live across SharePoint, OneDrive, Exchange Online and Teams, yet organizations must still prove how long they kept them and why they deleted them. This Simply Explained episode shows compliance teams and Microsoft 365 admins how Purview Records Management uses retention labels, record declaration, disposition review and audit history to build a defensible records lifecycle.
